Extract the weight matrix of a co-occurrence network

Source: R/converters.R
as_matrix.Rd

as_matrix() returns the weight matrix of a co-occurrence network built by cooccurrence(). The weight matrix is the network written as a square matrix with one row and one column per item, where a cell holds the weight of the edge between two items and the diagonal is zero. This form is what clustering, heatmaps, matrix algebra and many network packages expect, and it shows at once which item pairs never co-occur.

The cells hold the edge weights after similarity, scaling and filtering, or, with type = "raw", the number of transactions in which each pair co-occurs. The matrix agrees with the printed edge list, including any threshold or top_n filter. It is symmetric for every similarity except "relative", whose network is directed.

A result built with split_by stacks one network per group and has no single matrix, so group names the network to extract. For a graph object rather than a matrix, use as_igraph(), as_tidygraph(), as_cograph() or as_netobject().

Usage

as_matrix(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cooccurrence'
as_matrix(x, type = c("normalized", "raw"), group = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A cooccurrence edge list from cooccurrence().

...

Ignored.

type

"normalized" (default) for the edge weights, or "raw" for the co-occurrence counts.

group

For a result built with split_by, the name of the group to extract. NULL (default) for an unsplit result.

Value

A dense base numeric matrix with one row and one column per item, item names as row and column names, and a zero diagonal. Items that co-occur with nothing (isolates) keep a row of zeros. For similarity = "relative" the weight matrix is asymmetric: row i holds the weights of the edges from item i, and each non-empty row sums to 1 before filtering. The raw matrix is always symmetric.

Conditions

cooccure_grouped_input when x was built with split_by and group is NULL; cooccure_bad_input when group names no group of x, or is given for an unsplit result.

See also

cooccurrence() to build the network; as_igraph() for a graph object; as.data.frame.cooccurrence() for the edge and node tables.

Examples

net <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                    similarity = "jaccard", min_occur = 50)
as_matrix(net)

# One network of a split result
by_decade <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                          split_by = "decade", min_occur = 50)
as_matrix(by_decade, group = "2010s")
#>             Action Biography Comedy Crime Documentary Drama
